fields.name: datasets_used
fields.description: Any datasets, corpora, logs, benchmarks, participant data, prompts, or task materials used to develop, train, test, or evaluate the LLM-based HCI work.
fields.example: User study transcripts, ChatGPT interaction logs, UX workshop responses

fields.name: methods
fields.description: The study design, system approach, experimental setup, or analytical method used to investigate LLM use in HCI.
fields.example: Prototype system with mixed-method user study and comparative evaluation against baseline

fields.name: key_findings
fields.description: The main results, conclusions, or observed effects reported by the paper regarding LLM use in HCI.
fields.example: LLM support improved task completion and user satisfaction, but raised concerns about trust and controllability

fields.name: evaluation_metrics
fields.description: Any quantitative or qualitative metrics used to assess performance, usability, quality, or user experience.
fields.example: Accuracy, task completion rate, SUS, usability ratings, response quality scores

fields.name: hci_context
fields.description: The specific HCI setting, application area, or interaction scenario in which the LLM is used.
fields.example: UX education, conversational interface design, user research simulation

fields.name: llm_role
fields.description: How the large language model is used in the HCI system or study.
fields.example: User simulator, design assistant, conversational agent, coaching tool

fields.name: participants_or_users
fields.description: Who interacted with the system or took part in the study, including target users, designers, students, or other stakeholders.
fields.example: Undergraduate engineering students, UX practitioners, end users

fields.name: comparison_baseline
fields.description: Any baseline, control condition, or comparison system used in the study.
fields.example: Rule-based conversational agent, human coach, no-LLM baseline

fields.name: study_type
fields.description: The overall type of evidence provided by the paper.
fields.example: Proof-of-concept study, user study, system paper, evaluation study

fields.name: relevance_judgment
fields.description: Whether the paper provides substantive evidence relevant to using large language models in human-computer interaction within the HCI domain, based only on the title and abstract.
